People wear life jackets on a boat. Because the jacket holds a person up in the water even if she cannot swim or gets tired, it helps her stay afloat until help arrives.
Why can a kind word cheer up a sad classmate?
A kind word can help. Because it shows the classmate that someone has noticed and cares, he feels less alone with the sadness.
Why do people lower their voices when a baby is asleep in the room?
People speak softly. Because loud sounds can wake a sleeping baby, quiet voices let the baby and tired parents rest.
Why do people often feel cheerful on the morning of a holiday?
Holiday mornings feel cheerful. Because there is no rush to get anywhere and people have enjoyable things to look forward to, their minds feel light.
Why do two magnets sometimes push each other away?

Magnets push apart when the same ends face each other. Because each magnet has a north and a south end, and matching ends repel while different ends attract, turning one round changes the push into a pull.
Why does an iron gate rust but a gold ring does not?
The iron gate rusts. Because iron slowly reacts with water and air to make rust, while gold hardly reacts with anything, the ring stays shiny.
Why do owls come out at night?
Owls are active at night. Because they hunt small animals that move around after dark, and their large eyes and sharp hearing suit the dark, night is the best time for them to find food.
Why do spider webs sparkle on a misty morning?
Webs sparkle in the morning mist. Because tiny drops of water cling to the thin threads and each drop catches the light, the web glitters.
Why do some friends slowly drift apart?
Friends can drift apart. Because they spend less time together and their interests change, they have fewer things to share and the bond weakens.
Why does tea cool faster in a wide saucer than in a cup?
The tea cools faster in a saucer. Because a wide, shallow layer has more surface open to the air, more heat escapes and more water dries off.
Why does a pet dog rush to the door when its owner comes home?
The dog rushes to the door. Because it has bonded with its owner, it is glad to see the person and expects attention, and it may also hope for a walk or a treat.
Why does bread turn brown in a toaster?
Toast turns brown because strong heat changes the sugars and proteins on its surface. Because these react together, they make a brown colour and a new, toasty flavour.
Why does our stomach rumble when we have not eaten for a while?
The stomach rumbles because the gut keeps moving even when it is empty. Because its muscles squeeze air and liquid along, and no food is there to muffle the sound, we hear the noise.
Why do cactus plants have spines instead of ordinary leaves?
Spines suit a cactus. Because they lose far less water than broad leaves and also keep thirsty animals from eating the plant, the cactus can live in dry places.
Why do people say please when they ask for something?
Saying please makes a request polite. Because it shows respect for the other person and leaves them free to say yes, people are usually happier to help.
All roses are flowers, and all flowers need water. Do roses need water?
Yes, roses need water. Because roses are flowers and every flower needs water, the rule that covers all flowers covers roses too.
Why might a person laugh along with others who are teasing him even though it hurts?
He may laugh along. Because laughing can hide hurt feelings, help him fit in and avoid even more teasing, it feels like the safest choice at that moment.
Why does a group project go badly when one person does all the work?
The project suffers. Because that person gets tired and annoyed while the others learn nothing and feel they do not belong, the team stops working as a team.
Why do children take turns on a playground slide?
Taking turns is fair. Because everybody gets a chance and nobody has to push, there are fewer quarrels and fewer chances of someone being knocked over.
Why do shadows nearly vanish on a cloudy day?
Shadows fade under clouds. Because clouds scatter the sunlight so it reaches us from every part of the sky, there is no single bright spot to make a sharp dark patch.
Why does a see-saw tip down on the heavier child's side?
The see-saw tips towards the heavier child. Because the heavier child pulls the board down harder than the lighter child can pull the other side, the heavier end goes down.
Why does fog gather near a river on a cold morning?
Fog gathers because the air above the water cools. Because cool air cannot hold as much water vapour, the extra vapour turns into tiny floating droplets that we see as fog.
Why should seeds be sown before the rainy season rather than after it ends?
Sow them before the rains. Because the rain provides the water the seeds need to sprout and the plants to grow, they get a good start without extra watering.
Is it wrong to accept food from a stranger?
Do not take food from a stranger. Because you cannot be sure who prepared it or why it is being offered, a safe choice is to say no thank you and tell a trusted adult.
Why do small sounds seem louder at night?
Sounds seem louder at night mainly because everything else is quieter. Because there is less traffic and chatter to cover them, small noises stand out clearly.
Our neighbour's dog barks only at strangers. It barked at me yesterday. Am I a stranger to it?
Yes, I am a stranger to it. Because the dog barks only at strangers and it barked at me, the dog must see me as one.
What is sleep for?
Sleep lets the body and brain rest and recover. Because the body repairs itself and the brain sorts out what we learned during the day while we sleep, we feel clearer and stronger afterwards.
Why do roads in the hills wind in zigzags?
The roads zigzag to make the climb gentle. Because a straight road up a steep hill would be too steep for vehicles to climb safely, a winding path spreads the slope over a longer distance.
Why does a cut potato stay pale if we keep it in a bowl of water?
The potato stays pale because the water keeps air away from it. Because the dark colour comes from the cut surface reacting with air, covering it with water slows that change.
Why does a glass of water on a sunny windowsill sometimes throw a tiny rainbow on the wall?
The glass makes a rainbow because water bends sunlight. Because each colour in white light bends by a slightly different amount, the colours spread apart and land in separate stripes on the wall.
Why does our own voice sound different when we hear it on a recording?

Our voice sounds different because we normally hear it partly through our own head. Because the sound also travels through bone, it seems deeper to us, and a recording only carries the part that went through the air.
Why is it unsafe to swim in a river after heavy rain?

It is unsafe because the river becomes fast and unpredictable. Because rain adds a lot of water and makes the current strong and hides rocks and branches under the muddy surface, even good swimmers can be swept away.
Why do people often wear new clothes on a festival day?
New clothes show that the day is special. Because people like to mark an occasion with something fresh and good, wearing them adds to the feeling of celebration.
Why does paint peel off a wall that is damp?
The paint peels because water gets behind it. Because moisture pushes up from inside the wall and loosens the grip of the paint, the paint lifts in flakes.
Why do we feel bored in a long waiting room?
We feel bored because the mind has nothing interesting to hold its attention. Because attention keeps drifting to the passing time when nothing engages it, the minutes seem to crawl.
Why does it hurt when a friend forgets our name?
It hurts because a name is part of who we are. Because remembering it tells us someone paid attention to us, forgetting it makes us feel unnoticed.
Why do bees keep visiting flowers?
Bees visit flowers because they eat the sweet nectar. Because they brush against pollen while feeding and carry it from flower to flower, the plants can make seeds as a result.
If I leave a blown-up balloon on a sunny windowsill, why might it burst?
It might burst because the air inside gets hotter. Because warm air spreads out and pushes harder on the rubber, the thin skin is stretched past what it can take.
Why does water roll off a duck's back instead of soaking in?
Water rolls off because the feathers are oily. Because the oil makes the feathers repel water, the duck's body stays dry and warm even when it swims.
Does splitting a big project into small parts make it easier to finish, and why?
Splitting helps because each part feels doable. Because a huge task can seem too heavy to begin and small steps show quick progress, we keep going.
Why is it helpful to write the date at the top of each notebook page?
The date helps us find things later. Because notes are written over many days, the dates show the order of the lessons and make it easier to find a topic when we revise.
If the door is locked, the hall light stays off. Today the hall light is off. Is the door locked?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule only tells us what happens when the door is locked, the light could be off for another reason, such as a switch or a fault.
Why do children ask so many why questions?
Children ask because they are curious. Because the world is new to them and they want to understand how things work, asking is the quickest way to learn.
Why don't clouds fall down although they are made of water?

Clouds stay up because their drops are tiny and light. Because the droplets are so small that rising air keeps carrying them upwards, they drift instead of dropping, until they join into drops big enough to fall as rain.
What makes pushing a trolley up a ramp easier than lifting it straight up?
The ramp makes it easier. Because the trolley goes up in a long gentle slope instead of one steep climb, the push needed at any moment is smaller.
In a dusty room, why can we see the beam of a torch?
We see the beam because dust scatters some of the light. Because tiny specks send light in every direction, a little of it reaches our eyes from the side, and the path becomes visible.
Why do footballers wear boots with studs on the soles?
The studs give extra grip. Because they dig into the grass and stop the foot from sliding, a player can run and turn quickly without slipping.
Why does our face turn red after we run?
Our face turns red because more blood flows near the skin. Because running makes the body hot, the small blood vessels in the skin widen to let the heat escape into the air.
Why do families cook special dishes at festivals?
Special dishes mark the day as different from others. Because food made with extra care and shared with family feels like a treat, it makes the festival memorable.
Why do we get shy when many people are looking at us?
We get shy because we worry about being judged. Because attention makes us notice every small thing we say or do, we become self-conscious and stop feeling at ease.
Why can a dog respond to a whistle that people cannot hear?
The dog hears it because dog ears pick up higher sounds than ours. Because human hearing stops at a lower pitch, a very high whistle sounds like nothing to us but is clear to the dog.
All the pencils in this box are blue. Gita took one out of the box. What colour is her pencil?
Her pencil is blue. Because every pencil in the box is blue and hers came from that box, it must be blue.
Why do farmers plough a field before sowing seeds?
Farmers plough to loosen the soil. Because loose soil lets roots spread and lets air and water reach them, and ploughing also buries weeds, young plants grow better.
Why should we leave a little spare time between two tasks in our day?
Spare time is wise. Because tasks often take longer than we expect, a gap stops one delay from spoiling everything that comes next.
Why does a pot lid sometimes stay stuck to the pot after the food inside has cooled?

The lid stays stuck because the air pressure outside is pushing it down. Because the steam inside turned back into water as the pot cooled and left less pressure inside, the outside air presses the lid tight.
How does glue hold two pieces of paper together?
Glue holds paper because it sticks to the paper surfaces and then sets hard. Because it flows into the tiny gaps between the paper fibres before it dries, it locks the sheets together.
Why does a ceiling fan keep turning for a while after we switch it off?

The fan keeps turning because of inertia, the tendency of a moving thing to keep moving. Because the heavy blades carry a lot of motion and only friction in the bearings and air resistance slow them, they take a while to stop.
Why do some people find it hard to say no to their friends?
They find it hard because they fear upsetting the friend. Because people want to be liked and often worry that a refusal will end the friendship, they say yes even when they would rather not.
Why should we fly a kite far away from electric wires?
Kites must stay away from wires because of the danger of shock. Because a string or kite caught on a wire can carry electricity, especially if it is damp, the person holding it could be badly hurt.
Why do we learn a puzzle better by trying it ourselves than by only watching someone solve it?
Trying it ourselves works better. Because the mind learns most when it has to think and make mistakes, solving a puzzle ourselves fixes the steps in memory more than watching.
Why does a little sister want to join in all her elder brother's games?
She wants to join because she looks up to him. Because children enjoy doing what the people they admire do, being part of his game makes her feel grown up.
Why is the sand at the beach burning hot at noon while the sea water feels cool?
The sand gets hotter because it warms up much faster than water. Because water needs a lot more heat to change its temperature and also mixes the warmth into deeper water, the sea stays cool.
Why does a caterpillar eat leaves almost all day?
A caterpillar eats all day because it must grow. Because it will later change into a butterfly or moth and cannot feed much during the change, it stores up food while it can.
Thick card is easier to cut with scissors near the hinge. Why?

It is easier near the hinge because the blades press harder on the card there. Because the blades act like a lever, the same push at the handles gives a bigger squeeze on the card the closer it is to the pivot.
Why do people arrive at the railway station well before the train leaves?
They arrive early because trains do not wait. Because there may be a queue, a platform to find or a delay on the way, extra time keeps them from missing the train.
Why do players warm up before a match?
Players warm up to get the body ready. Because gentle exercise loosens the muscles and sends more blood to them, they move better and are less likely to be strained.
Why do we cough when a crumb goes down the wrong way?
We cough because the body is trying to clear the airway. Because a crumb in the windpipe blocks air and sets off a reflex, a strong push of air is sent out to throw it back up.
Why do soap bubbles show swirling colours?

Bubbles show colours because of how light bounces off their thin skin. Because light reflects from the front and the back of the soapy film and the reflections mix, some colours grow stronger while others fade.
Why does a bush grow bushier when the gardener snips its tips?
The bush grows bushier because side buds start to grow. Because the tip of a shoot holds back the buds below it, cutting it off lets them grow into new branches.
Anyone with a ticket may enter the hall. Nina walked in. Must she have a ticket?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule says people with tickets may enter but does not say that nobody else may, Nina may have been let in for some other reason.
Why do picnic organisers write a list of who brings what?
A list prevents mistakes. Because without it several people might bring the same dish while nobody brings plates, and with it every need is covered once.
Why does a train horn sound higher as the train comes nearer and lower once it has passed?

The horn changes pitch because the train is moving. Because the sound waves are squeezed together as the train comes towards us and stretched apart as it goes away, our ears hear a higher note and then a lower one.
Why do small lamps look so bright on a dark evening?
The lamps look bright because everything around them is dark. Because our eyes judge brightness by comparison and adjust to the dim surroundings, even a tiny flame stands out.
A friend is upset with me. What is a sensible first step?

A good first step is to talk to the friend calmly and listen. Because anger usually fades when a person feels understood, hearing their side gives us a chance to say sorry if we were wrong and fix things.
Why is a family meal a good time to talk?
A shared meal is good for talking because everyone sits together without hurry. Because there are no other tasks pulling attention away, people can tell each other about their day.
Why does ironing smooth out the creases in a shirt?
Ironing smooths the shirt because of heat and pressing. Because warm fibres become soft and can be flattened, and they stay that way as they cool, the creases disappear.
Is revising a lesson on the day it was taught really better? Why?
It is better because we forget quickly. Because new facts fade from memory unless they are used again, a quick look soon afterwards helps them stay.
Why should a toaster be unplugged before we clean it?
It should be unplugged to prevent an electric shock. Because the heating parts inside are connected to the mains, cleaning around them while the power is on could give a dangerous jolt.
Why does a cool breeze blow from the sea towards the land in the afternoon?
The breeze blows in because the land has become warmer than the sea. Because warm air above the land rises and cooler air from the sea moves in to fill the space, we feel a breeze from the water.
Why does a cat usually land on its feet when it falls?

A cat usually lands on its feet because its body twists in the air. Because cats have very flexible spines and a quick sense of balance, they turn their bodies the right way up before they reach the ground.
Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker?
Food cooks faster because the water inside gets hotter than usual. Because the closed lid traps steam and raises the pressure, the water boils at a higher temperature and softens the food sooner.
Why is the door handle fixed far from the hinge?
The handle is far from the hinge so the door is easy to push. Because force applied far from the pivot turns the door more easily, a light push is enough.
Why are there speed bumps on the road near a school?
Speed bumps make drivers slow down. Because a fast car jolts badly over a bump, drivers ease off, and children crossing the road are much safer from slow traffic.
What makes some people short-tempered when they are hungry?
Hunger can make people short-tempered because the body lacks fuel. Because tired, hungry people have less patience and self-control, small annoyances seem much bigger.
My wooden cupboard door sticks in the monsoon but opens easily in winter. What is going on?
The door sticks because the wood has swollen a little. Because wood soaks up water from the damp monsoon air, it expands and rubs against the frame, and it shrinks again when the air dries.
Why do runners stay in their own lanes on a track?
Runners stay in their lanes to keep the race fair. Because jostling or cutting across would slow other runners and give some an unfair gain, lanes give each person a clear path.
Why do people have two eyes and not just one?
Eyes working as a pair help us judge how far away things are. Because each eye sees from a slightly different spot, the brain compares the pictures and works out depth.
Why do road signs glow in the headlights of a car at night, though they have no bulbs?
The signs glow because they are coated to send light back where it came from. Because the coating sends the headlight beam straight back towards the car, the driver sees a bright sign.
Lena says the film must be good because the audience clapped at the end. Is she certain about that?
No, she cannot be certain. Because people may clap to be polite or because they are glad it is over, clapping alone does not prove that the film was good.
Why do people check the weather report before planning a picnic?
They check the report so the picnic is not ruined. Because rain or strong heat would make the day unpleasant, knowing in advance lets them pick a better day.
Why do the leaves of a plant droop when the soil gets very dry?
The leaves droop because they lose their firmness. Because plant cells stay stiff when they are full of water, a plant with too little water in its soil goes limp.
Why might a classmate not want to talk about a bad exam result?
The classmate may feel embarrassed. Because a poor result can seem like a sign of failure, talking about it brings the unpleasant feeling back, so they would rather keep quiet.
Why do we keep a doormat outside the front door?
The mat catches dirt. Because shoes carry mud and dust and rubbing them on the mat removes much of it, less dirt gets carried onto the floor inside.
Why do people share sweets with their neighbours during festivals?
Sharing sweets spreads the joy. Because giving something nice shows that we care about those who live near us, it builds friendship and good feeling in the lane.
Why do families keep old photographs?
Families keep photographs to remember. Because a picture can bring back a person, a place or a day that has slipped from memory, it keeps those times close.
Why does a pulley make it easier to lift a bucket from a well?
A pulley makes lifting easier by changing the direction of the pull. Because you pull down on the rope and can use your own weight, it is more comfortable than lifting the bucket straight up.
Why does a quiet corner help a student prepare for exams?
A quiet corner helps because there is less to distract the mind. Because attention is easily pulled away by noise and movement, a calm place lets us stay with the work for longer.
Why does a hot pan spit and hiss when a few drops of water fall into the oil?
The pan spits because the water turns to steam at once. Because water is heavier than oil and sinks to the bottom of the hot pan, it boils violently there and throws the oil upwards.
Why should children never play near an open well?
Children should stay away because a fall could be very dangerous. Because an open well is deep and the sides are hard to climb out of, a child who falls in might not get out alone.
Why do frogs start croaking loudly after the first rains?
Frogs croak after the rains because it is their time to find mates. Because ponds and puddles fill up with water where eggs can be laid, the male frogs call to attract females.
Why does wet mud turn hard and crack under the hot sun?
The mud hardens because the water in it dries away. Because the tiny clay grains stick tightly together as the water leaves and the mud shrinks, the ground splits into cracks.
Why does a small boat rock when a big boat passes by?
The small boat rocks because of the waves. Because the big boat pushes water aside as it moves and makes ripples that spread out and reach the small boat, it is lifted and dropped as they pass.
Why does music from a closed room sound dull and boomy from outside?
The music sounds dull because the wall lets low notes through more easily. Because walls stop the sharp, high sounds better than the deep ones, mostly the thumping bass reaches us.
Why does a nail left near the sea rust faster than one kept far inland?

The seaside nail rusts faster because of the salt in the air. Because salt dissolves in the thin film of damp on the metal and helps the rusting change happen more quickly, the iron wears away sooner.
Why can one small act of kindness cheer us up on a bad day?
A small kindness cheers us up because it shows someone cares. Because feeling cared for makes problems seem easier to carry, the day looks less bleak.
Why can we see a glowing lamp from far away at night but not an unlit one?

The lamp is visible because it makes its own light. Because an unlit object is seen only when other light bounces off it into our eyes and the night has so little of that, it disappears into the dark.
Nobody in the school choir is late today. Hari is in the choir. Is Hari late?
No, Hari is not late. Because no member of the choir is late and Hari is a member, he must be on time.
Why do we squint when we step into bright sunshine?
We squint because it lets in less light. Because narrowing the eyelids cuts down the amount of light reaching the eye, the glare hurts less and we can see better.
Why do heavy curtains help to keep a room cooler in the afternoon?
Heavy curtains help because they keep the sun out. Because sunlight coming through a window turns into heat inside a room, blocking it before it enters leaves the room cooler.
Why is it good to listen to a friend's problem without interrupting?
Listening quietly is good because it shows we care. Because people want to feel heard before they want advice, letting them finish tells them we take their worry seriously.
What are the lines we see on a leaf for?
The lines are tiny pipes called veins. Because they carry water to every part of the leaf and carry the food the leaf makes away to the rest of the plant, the leaf can stay alive and flat.
Why do players from opposing teams shake hands after a match?
They shake hands to show good sportsmanship. Because the game was a contest and not a quarrel, the handshake tells everyone that they respect each other whatever the result.
Why do kites fly best on a windy day?
Kites need wind to rise. Because moving air pushes against the tilted kite and lifts it, a calm day leaves the kite hanging limply.
Why do screws usually hold wood better than nails?
Screws usually hold better because of their threads. Because the spiral ridges bite into the wood and must be turned back out and not simply pulled, they resist being pulled free.
Why should a child tell an adult at once when they see smoke in the house?
The child should tell an adult because smoke may mean a fire. Because a small fire can spread fast and an adult knows how to get everyone out safely, quick news saves time.
Why does cooked rice stick together in a lump?
Rice sticks because of starch. Because grains give out sticky starch as they cook in water, the starch acts like a glue between the grains when they cool.
Why does the same rule apply to every child in a school?
The same rule applies to everyone to keep things fair. Because children would feel cheated if some of them could do what others were not allowed to do, equal rules build trust.
Why is a clear night usually colder than a cloudy night?
A clear night is colder. Because clouds act like a blanket and hold the day's warmth near the ground, while on a clear night the heat escapes straight into the sky, the ground cools more.
Why does a tin-can telephone only work when the string is pulled tight?

The string must be tight because the sound travels along it as a shaking. Because a loose string sags and soaks up the shakes instead of passing them on, the voice fades before it reaches the other can.
Why do parents repeat the same reminders many times?
Parents repeat reminders because they want things to be done. Because children often forget or are busy with other things, a gentle repeat helps them remember.
Friends are coming to lunch tomorrow. Should I tidy the house tonight or leave it for the last moment?
Tidy most of it tonight. Because a rushed clean-up in the morning leaves no time for cooking and a last-minute problem, and tonight's work lets you stay calm when the guests arrive.
Why does an aeroplane need a very long runway?

The runway must be long because the plane has to reach a high speed. Because a plane lifts off only when it moves fast enough for the air under its wings to hold it, it needs plenty of ground to build up that speed.
Why do small fish swim together in large groups?
Fish swim in groups for safety. Because a predator finds it hard to pick out one fish from a moving crowd, and many eyes notice danger sooner, each fish is less likely to be caught.
Why does a sheet of paper tear so easily after it gets soaked in water?
Wet paper tears easily because it loses much of its strength. Because water gets in between the fibres and loosens the bonds that hold them together, they slide apart with only a small pull.
After telling a lie to a friend, why do we feel bad?
We feel bad because we know we have been unfair to them. Because lying breaks trust, and most people care about being honest with those they like, the guilt stays with us.
Why do sunglasses make a bright afternoon easier on the eyes?
Sunglasses make it easier because they let less light through. Because the dark lenses block part of the glare before it reaches the eye, the eyes do not have to squint so much.
Why do our legs feel heavy after climbing many stairs?
Our legs feel heavy because the muscles have worked hard. Because working muscles use up their fuel and gather tiring waste in them, they cannot pull as strongly until they have rested.
The red box is heavier than the green box, and the blue box is lighter than the green box. Which box is the heaviest?
The red box is the heaviest. Because the red box is heavier than the green one and the green one is heavier than the blue one, red is above the others.
Why does a vegetable patch grow badly when weeds are left to take over?
The vegetables grow badly because the weeds compete with them. Because weeds use up water, light and nutrients in the soil, there is less left for the plants we want.
Why does a rolling ball slow down and stop on a grass field?
The ball slows down because the grass rubs against it. Because this rubbing, called friction, works against the motion and takes away its energy, the ball comes to rest.
Why do schools hold rehearsals before the annual function?
Rehearsals help the function to go smoothly. Because every child learns when to come on and what to do, and mistakes can be fixed in advance, the real show has fewer surprises.
Why should matches be kept out of the reach of small children?
Matches should be kept away because a flame can cause burns or a fire. Because small children are curious and do not understand the danger, they may strike a match just to see what happens.
Why do clothes smell damp when they dry indoors during the monsoon?
The clothes smell damp because they stay wet for a long time. Because the humid air takes away water slowly, tiny germs can grow in the cloth and make that smell.
Why does dosa batter rise and bubble when left overnight?
The batter rises because tiny living yeast and bacteria grow in it. Because they feed on the sugars in the batter and give off gas, the gas puffs it up with bubbles.
How does a car stay on the road when it goes round a bend?

The car stays on the road because of the grip between the tyres and the ground. Because this friction pulls the car towards the inside of the curve instead of letting it slide straight on, the car turns.
Why does a school have a bell?
The bell tells everyone the same thing at the same time. Because a loud, clear sound can be heard in every corner of the building, students and teachers know when to begin and finish the lessons.
Why is it a good idea to leave a spare key with a trusted neighbour?
A spare key with a neighbour is a good idea. Because the neighbour can open the door if we lose our own key or lock ourselves out, we are not stranded.
Why is it colder at the top of a mountain than in the valley below?
It is colder at the top because the air there is thinner. Because thin air holds less heat, and the warm ground that heats the air in the valley is far below, the mountain top stays chilly.
Is it fair to judge a classmate by one bad day?
No, it is not fair. Because one bad day shows only a small part of a person and anyone can be tired or upset, we need to see how they usually behave before we decide.
Why can we hear a person talking in the next room even though we cannot see them?

We hear the person because sound travels in ways light cannot. Because sound slips through gaps and around corners and shakes thin walls, while light travels straight and is blocked by the wall, we hear without seeing.
Why do tyres have grooves cut into the rubber?
The grooves help the tyre grip the road. Because they give water somewhere to go as the tyre rolls and give the rubber little edges to bite, the tyre does not skid as easily in the wet.
Why are people so curious about a closed gift box?
People are curious because they do not know what is inside. Because the mind likes to fill in missing knowledge and the box hides the answer, the wish to find out grows stronger.
Why does a baby smile at familiar faces more than at strangers?
The baby smiles because the faces are known and make it feel safe. Because babies learn quickly who cares for them and relax in their company, they show happiness to those people.
Why do elephants spray mud or dust on their backs?
Elephants cover themselves to protect their skin. Because a coat of mud keeps off the sun and cools the skin, and it keeps biting insects away, the elephant stays comfortable.
Why do railway tracks have tiny gaps between their sections?
The gaps leave room for the steel to grow. Because metal expands when the sun heats it, joined rails with no gaps would push against each other and bend out of shape.
Why do tall buildings appear upside down in a still puddle?

The reflection looks upside down because water works like a mirror. Because light from the top of the building travels down to the surface and bounces up to our eyes at a slant, the top appears at the lowest part of the picture.
Why can't a person tickle themselves?

A person cannot tickle themselves because the brain expects the touch. Because the brain knows what the hand will do before it does it and so treats the feeling as harmless, the surprise that makes tickling funny is missing.
Mira, Raju and Sam sit in a row. Mira is to the left of Raju, and Raju is to the left of Sam. Who sits in the middle?
Raju sits in the middle. Because Mira is to his left and Sam is to his right, he is between them.
Why does a cut flower last longer when it is kept in a vase of water?
The flower lasts longer because its stem keeps drinking. Because water travels up thin tubes inside the stem to the petals and leaves, the flower stays fresh instead of drying out.
Why should children keep away from a building site?
Building sites are dangerous. Because there are heavy objects, open holes and moving machines and workers cannot always see small children, a child might easily be hurt.
Why are roads slippery in the first few minutes of a rain shower?
The road is slippery because rain mixes with the dust and oil on it. Because this thin muddy film sits between the tyres and the road, the grip is poor until more rain washes it away.
Why do we have day and night?
We have day and night because the Earth spins. Because the Earth turns all the way round every day, the side facing the sun has daylight while the side turned away is dark.
Why does a firecracker make such a sudden loud bang?
The bang comes from a quick burst of gas. Because the burning powder makes a lot of hot gas in a flash and the gas shoves the air outward sharply, we hear a loud crack.
How does a mosquito net protect a sleeping person?
The net protects by keeping mosquitoes away. Because its tiny holes are too small for the insects to pass through, they cannot reach the skin to bite.
Why does a big drum sound deeper than a small one?
The big drum sounds deeper because its skin shakes more slowly. Because a larger, heavier skin takes longer to move back and forth, it makes a lower note than a small, tight skin.
Why do students feel proud when their drawing is put up on the classroom wall?
They feel proud because their effort is noticed. Because people like to see that their work matters to others, a display tells them that what they made is worth showing.
Why do high jumpers land on thick soft mats?
They land on mats to avoid injury. Because a soft mat slows the jumper gently over a longer time than hard ground would, the force on the body is much smaller.
Why do friends often grow closer after finishing a hard task together?
They grow closer because they shared an effort. Because working through difficulty side by side builds trust, and each person sees the others being helpful, the bond becomes stronger.
Why is it sensible to plan the route before a long cycle ride with friends?
Planning the route is sensible. Because everyone then knows where to go and where to stop for rest, nobody gets lost or left behind.
Why do we soak dried chickpeas before cooking them?
We soak chickpeas to make them cook quicker. Because the hard dry seeds take in water and swell, they are already part-softened before they go on the stove.
How can we feel lonely in a crowded place?
We can feel lonely in a crowd because loneliness depends on connection and not company. Because being surrounded by strangers does not give us anyone who knows or cares about us, we feel apart.
Why does a torch fail to light if one battery is put in the wrong way round?
The torch fails because the electricity cannot flow properly. Because the batteries must be placed so that their positive and negative ends line up in the circuit, a reversed battery blocks the flow.
Why do parents ask us to tell them once we reach a friend's house?
They ask because they want to know we are safe. Because a short message ends their worry at once, it is a small way to give them peace.
Why does a dog sniff everything on its walk?
A dog sniffs because smell is its main way of learning about the world. Because a dog's nose is far more sensitive than ours, each sniff tells it who has passed that way and what food is nearby.
Why does a ceramic cup shatter on a stone floor while a steel cup only gets a dent?
The ceramic cup shatters because it is hard but cannot bend. Because steel bends a little under a knock and absorbs the force, it dents instead of breaking.
A thin curtain lets in daylight but a thick one makes the room dark. Why is that?
The thick curtain makes the room darker. Because closely woven heavy cloth blocks most of the light, while thin cloth has tiny gaps and passes some through, the thin curtain only dims the room.
Why do we feel no pain when we trim the ends of our fingernails?
Trimming does not hurt because the tip of the nail has no feeling. Because the nerves lie in the skin underneath and not in the hard nail itself, the cut ends are like dry hair.
Why should we walk slowly on a freshly mopped floor?
We should walk slowly because the floor is slippery. Because a thin layer of water cuts down the grip between shoes and the floor, a quick step can slide away and cause a fall.
Why do people decorate their doorways with flowers and rangoli during festivals?
They decorate to welcome visitors and show joy. Because a bright, pretty entrance tells guests they are expected and the family has taken trouble for them, the house feels festive.
Why do teachers give homework?
Homework gives students practice. Because skills grow stronger when we use them again and again, working at home helps a lesson settle in the mind.
Why do some seeds have little wings or soft fluff?
Wings and fluff help seeds travel. Because the wind can carry such light parts a long way, the seeds land away from the parent plant and have room to grow.
Why do rivers always flow downhill?
Rivers flow downhill because gravity pulls water down. Because water is free to move and the ground slopes towards the sea, it keeps running to the lowest place it can reach.
Why does a friend feel hurt when we cancel our plans at the last minute?

The friend feels hurt because the cancellation feels like being unimportant. Because they may have saved time for us and looked forward to the meeting, a sudden change feels like their time was not valued.
Why do fresh green leaves turn limp when left on a hot kitchen counter?
The leaves go limp because they lose water. Because warm air dries them and plant cells are firm only when full of water, they lose their crispness.
Either the cat or the dog ate the biscuit, not both. The dog was out of the house when it vanished. Who ate it?
The cat ate it. Because it was the cat or the dog and the dog was not in the house, the dog could not have eaten it.
How can the taps in a house get water from a tank on the roof without a pump?
The water flows because of gravity. Because the tank is higher than the taps and water always runs towards lower places, it pushes through the pipes and out of the taps.
Why does a flute give a higher note when more of its holes are left open?
The note gets higher because the shaking column of air gets shorter. Because a short column of air shakes faster than a long one, the pitch we hear goes up.
Why do bus drivers slow down at sharp turns?
Drivers slow down because the bus could skid or tip. Because a moving vehicle wants to keep going straight and the tyres can only grip so much, a sharp turn at speed is dangerous.
Why do goalkeepers wear gloves?
Goalkeepers wear gloves for grip and protection. Because the rough surface of the glove helps hold a slippery ball and the padding softens the hit, saves are easier and less painful.
Our class cannot agree on where to go for the annual trip because everyone wants a different place. How should we decide?
The class should hold a vote. Because every student gets a say and the result is clear, most people will accept it as fair even if their own choice does not win.
Why do bicycles have gears?
Gears help the rider cope with different ground. Because a low gear makes the pedals easy to push uphill and a high gear gives more speed on flat roads, the rider can save effort.
Why do deer and rabbits have eyes on the sides of their heads?
Their eyes sit on the sides so they can see almost all around. Because these animals are hunted, spotting danger coming from any direction gives them time to run.
A candle melts over a small flame, but a steel bowl does not. Why?

The candle melts because wax needs only a little heat to turn liquid. Because steel needs a far higher temperature before it melts, an ordinary flame cannot change the bowl, though it can make it hot.
Why do cousins who meet only on holidays often feel close?
They feel close because they share family stories and fun. Because they play together in a relaxed way and belong to the same family, they feel at ease with each other even after long gaps.
Why does a sad song sometimes make a sad person feel a little better?
A sad song can help because it shows that someone else has felt the same way. Because feeling understood is a comfort, the sadness seems lighter and easier to share.
How do spectacles help a person see clearly?

Spectacles help because the lenses change the path of the light. Because the curved glass bends the light before it enters the eye, the picture lands sharply at the back of the eye instead of blurred.
Why is it better to water the garden in the evening than at noon?
Evening is better because less water is lost. Because the sun is weaker and the air is cooler, less of the water dries into the air and more soaks down to the roots.
Why does butter melt so fast on a hot paratha?
Butter melts quickly because it needs very little heat. Because the fat in butter turns liquid at a low temperature, the heat from the paratha softens it within seconds.
Why do new friends ask each other so many questions?
They ask many questions to get to know one another. Because they have not yet shared any history, questions are the quickest way to find what they like and what they have in common.
Some of the books on the shelf are new. Can we say that every book on the shelf is new?
No, we cannot say that. Because the word some tells us only that at least a part of them are new, it says nothing about the rest, which may be old or new.
Why does water in a clay pot stay cooler than in a steel bottle on a hot day?
The clay pot keeps water cooler because it lets a little water seep out. Because that water dries from the outside and drying takes heat away from the pot, the water inside gets colder.
Why do people carry a water bottle on a long road trip?
They carry water because the journey can be long and tiring. Because there may be no shop for a long stretch and the body needs drink when it is hot, a bottle saves the travellers from thirst.
Why do we check the brakes of a bicycle before riding down a long slope?
We check the brakes because the bicycle speeds up on a slope. Because gravity pulls it faster and faster, a rider with poor brakes cannot slow down or stop in time.
Why do swimmers often wear a cap?
A cap helps a swimmer move faster. Because loose hair drags in the water and slows the swimmer down, covering it keeps the head smooth.
Why are chairs usually kept ready for the elders at a festival gathering?
Chairs are kept for elders out of respect and comfort. Because older people tire sooner when standing for long, a seat lets them enjoy the event.
Why is it easier to loosen a tight nut with a long spanner than a short one?
A long spanner makes it easier. Because a longer handle gives the hand more leverage, a small push at the end turns the nut with a bigger twist.
Why does a ringing bell go silent the moment you touch it with your hand?
The bell goes silent because your hand stops its shaking. Because sound is made by the metal vibrating, and your hand holds the metal still, nothing is left to push the air.
The morning will be sunny and the afternoon rainy, and I have a heavy blanket to dry outside. When should I hang it out?
Hang it out first thing in the morning. Because a heavy blanket needs the longest stretch of sun to dry, and starting early lets it dry fully before the rain arrives.
Why does a snake keep flicking its tongue in and out?

The snake flicks its tongue to smell its surroundings. Because the tongue picks up tiny particles from the air and the ground and brings them to special organs in the mouth, the snake can find food and sense danger.
Why does lightning often hit tall trees or towers?
Tall things are struck more often because they stand closer to the cloud. Because the electricity looks for the easiest and shortest path to the ground, a tall tree gives it a good one.
Why does a glass jar sometimes crack when boiling water is poured into it straight from a cold shelf?
The jar can crack because one part heats much faster than the rest. Because the inner glass swells quickly while the outer glass is still cold and small, the strain between them pulls the jar apart.
Why do parents worry when their child is late coming home?
Parents worry because they care about our safety. Because they cannot see where we are and do not know why we are late, their minds fill with possible problems until we are home.
Why does reading your own writing aloud help you spot mistakes?
Reading aloud helps because we hear the sentence slowly. Because our eyes tend to skip over errors when we read silently and fast, our ears notice words that sound wrong or missing.
After a hard test is over, why do we feel relieved?
We feel relieved because the worry has ended. Because the mind has been tense while waiting for the test, the body relaxes once the pressure is gone.
Why does our mouth water when we smell hot pakoras?
Our mouth waters because the body gets ready to eat. Because the smell tells the brain that food is near, the brain signals the glands in the mouth to make spit, which helps to break down food.
Why does a tree have such thick bark?
The thick bark protects the tree. Because the tough outer layer shields the soft living wood from heat, knocks, and tiny insects, the tree can live for many years.
Why do frozen vegetables turn soft and watery after they thaw?
The vegetables turn soft because freezing damages them. Because water inside the cells turns into sharp ice crystals that break the cell walls, the pieces cannot stay firm when they warm up.
Do good friends have to agree about everything?
No, good friends do not have to agree about everything. Because a friendship rests on trust and respect and not on matching opinions, friends can disagree politely and still enjoy each other.
Why is a loose scarf a bad idea when riding on a motorbike or near a machine?
A loose scarf is risky because it can get caught. Because a flapping end may be pulled into a wheel or machine part, it can yank the wearer along with it.
Why do people stand in a queue at a crowded festival stall?
A queue keeps things fair and orderly. Because people are served in the order they came, nobody can push ahead, and there is less pushing and shouting.
Why does a house with thick walls stay cooler in summer?
Thick walls keep the house cooler. Because the heat from the sun takes a long time to travel through the wall to the inside, the rooms stay comfortable well into the afternoon.
Why does practising with the weaker hand help a player become better with both?
Practising helps because skills are learned by repetition. Because the brain and muscles get better at any movement they repeat, the weaker hand slowly catches up.
Why do we clean a wall before painting it?
We clean the wall first so the paint will last. Because paint holds well on a clean, dry surface but slips off dust or grease, a dirty wall makes the new coat peel.
Why is a house with a tin roof usually hotter inside than one with a clay-tile roof?
A tin roof makes the house hotter. Because metal soaks up the sun's heat and passes it straight through, while thick tiles pass it on slowly, the room under the tin heats up sooner.
Why is a room with heavy curtains and thick carpets quieter than a bare room?
Soft furnishings make the room quieter. Because cloth and carpet take in sound instead of bouncing it back, there are fewer echoes and the noise dies away quickly.
Why do birds build nests?
Birds build nests to give their eggs and chicks a safe place. Because eggs need warmth and shelter and a nest keeps them off the ground, away from many dangers, more chicks survive.
Why is it better to ask the teacher when you are stuck than to guess and move on?
Asking is better because it clears up the problem at once. Because a guess may be wrong and later lessons often depend on earlier ones, a small gap can grow bigger if it is left alone.
Every student who wins the quiz gets a medal. Kiran has a medal. Did Kiran win the quiz?
We cannot be sure. Because the rule says winners get medals but does not say that only winners do, Kiran may have earned his medal in another way.
Why is it fair for every person in the house to help with the chores?
It is fair because everyone uses the house. Because the work will pile up on one person if the rest do nothing, sharing the tasks keeps any one person from being worn out.
Why does laughing make a bad mood feel lighter?
Laughing lightens the mood because it breaks the grip of worry. Because it takes our attention off the problem for a moment and relaxes the body, we feel better afterwards.
Why is the soil next to a river often good for farming?
The soil is good because the river brings fertile mud. Because floods leave behind a fine layer of silt rich in nutrients from far upstream, the plants growing there find plenty of food.
Why does a mirror show a clear picture of your face while a plain wall does not?

The mirror shows a clear picture because its surface is very smooth. Because smooth glass sends light back in an orderly way, while a rough wall scatters it in all directions, only the mirror keeps the shape of your face.
Why does a fuse cut off the electricity when too much power flows through it?
A fuse protects the wires. Because too much current heats a wire and can start a fire, the thin fuse wire melts first and breaks the circuit.
Why do people tie a name tag on their luggage?
A tag helps to identify the bag. Because many bags look alike and a tag shows who owns each one, a bag that goes astray can be returned to its owner.
Why do we pull our hand away from a hot pan before we have even thought about it?

The hand moves because of a quick reflex. Because the message of heat is handled by the spinal cord, which sends back an order to move without waiting for the brain to decide, the hand is saved a moment earlier.
